fixes.explanation: It's actually true, friend. Moses says, “Your sons and daughters will be given to another nation, while your eyes grow weary looking for them day after day, with no power in your hand.” (Deuteronomy 28:32). I think this is one of the hardest lines in the whole list. The ones looking grow weary day after day, with no power in their hand.

Yes, baker. Moses says, “…there you will worship other gods—gods of wood and stone.” (Deuteronomy 28:36). It's a nation neither they nor their fathers have known. Wood and stone are what he names for those gods.

Not quite, friend. Moses says, “…you will serve your enemies the LORD will send against you…” (Deuteronomy 28:48). The word is enemies. Neighbors aren't in the verse, and the ones the LORD sends are called enemies.

Yes, baker. Moses describes “…a nation whose language you will not understand…” (Deuteronomy 28:49). He says the LORD will bring it from afar, from the ends of the earth, to swoop down like an eagle. Israel won't understand its language.
